Write two versions of the "Caching and retries" section of the HTTP API spec for `ordersvc`, from the same facts. Output each version under its label (### 1 and ### 2) and nothing else.

### 1. Public spec
The public spec does not use RFC 2119 keywords.

### 2. Internal spec
The internal spec starts with this sentence: "The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119."

Facts:
- Clients are allowed to cache a `GET /orders/{id}` response for up to 60 seconds.
- Clients are required to send an `Idempotency-Key` header with every `POST /orders` request.
- Clients are able to resume an interrupted upload with a `Range` header. The server supports this from v2.3 on.
- Clients are advised to use exponential backoff after a `429` response.
- The server is required to NEVER return a cached response to a `POST` request.

Edit the pull request description below. Keep every fact, both headings and all code; change only the wording. Output only the edited description.

## Summary

This PR adds a robust, seamless retry mechanism that serves as the backbone of the upload client. In order to reduce failed uploads, the client now uses exponential backoff. Due to the fact that the old client retried immediately, it had the ability to overload the server in the event that the server was slow. The new upload client retry backoff cap is 30 seconds.

## Testing

It is important to note that the new test case covers the edge case where the server returns `503` three times in a row. The feature flag `upload.retry_v2` gates the new behavior, and it is very easy to turn off. In many cases, retries finish in real-time, and the metrics on the dashboard stay up-to-date. The well documented `RetryPolicy` type boasts a configurable cap.
